notes: Reference corpus; deliverables in research/corpora/rpatters1-main/. Published findings cite it. 1149 distinct source hashes across 1288 loose files; 2042 exports present, 1189 matched adjacent-exact, 99 unmatched. Archive members included: 2437 occurrences, from 509 archives. corpus_fingerprint covers loose files only, so it is comparable across runs with and without archives. Surveyed without --sniff-content: every source here is named *.mus. Re-surveyed 2026-08-12 for two reasons, and the count fell from 1289 to 1288 accordingly. First, one specimen is excluded by name in the private survey configuration: mus-851e50ffa96534f6 is a classic-Mac Microsoft Word document (signature 0xFE37 0x0023) carrying a misleading .mus extension, and the reader correctly refuses it. Second, inventory.py no longer falls back to a corpus-wide basename search when a source has no companion at its conventional path. The 36 fallback-unique and 29 fallback-ambiguous pairings reported by the previous run were guesses, not pairings, and are now reported as missing. The 1189 adjacent-exact pairs are unchanged.

Finale application installations for macOS and Windows, Finale 1.0.0 through Finale 2011, rather than authored documents; deliverables in research/corpora/rpatters1-installs/. 4536 distinct source hashes across 12116 loose files, so this corpus is heavily duplicated across versions. Surveyed with --sniff-content, without which the classic Mac eras would be invisible: those documents kept the file type in the resource fork and carry no extension. corpus_fingerprint covers loose files only. This corpus now has exports and the semantic half of the pipeline runs: 3090 adjacent-exact companions, being 3066 Finale 2011 documents and the 24 WinFin 2.2 tutorial files. Its companion convention is a '-finale27' directory holding '<stem>.musx', which is NOT the '-exports'/'.fin27.musx' convention rpatters1-main uses. Re-surveyed 2026-08-12 after the Finale 2011 install DVD was imaged and its Mac and Windows payloads mined (count rose from 9764 to 12116). Finale 2011 is version 16.0.0.30, previously unverified in VERSION_MATRIX.md. Excluded: 'Finale PDK' (MakeMusic proprietary, outside this project's provenance boundary); '*.lib', '*.fan' and '*.fpa'; the Finale 2014.5/25/26/27 application bundles (MUSX-era only); and '*/Libraries*', which holds Finale's setting libraries rather than scores and contributed ~900 specimens no era framing classifies. KEEP='*Default*' re-admits the stock font-default files that live inside that excluded tree; the pattern is not '*Font Default*' because 'Handwritten Default' and 'Default Fonts' carry no such substring. Those files still classify under no epoch and recover nothing, which is a reader gap and the reason to keep them visible. inventory.py no longer falls back to a corpus-wide basename search: in a corpus of repeated installs the same filename recurs in every version directory by design, and the previous run's 7266 fallback-ambiguous and 112 fallback-unique pairings were all false, every one of them matching some other version's source to a Finale 2011 export.

Controlled fixtures committed to this repository, surveyed as a corpus in their own right; deliverables in research/corpora/tracked-evidence/. 70 loose *.mus files, all 70 distinct by content and all 70 paired adjacent-exact with a Finale 27 companion, which is the highest companion coverage of any survey and the reason this cohort exists. Its unique contribution is the earliest era: both private corpora begin at Finale 1.8.7, so the only companion-backed Finale 1.0.0 evidence in any survey is the 20 fixtures here, along with the controlled one-variable edit pairs that no authored corpus can supply. Products present: 1.0.0 (20), 2.6 (5), 3.7 (7), 97 (5), 2000 (2), 2002 (3), 2003 (2), 2004b (2), 2005 (11), 2006 (5), 2007 (1), 2012 (7). Its companion convention is a '-finale27' directory holding '<stem>.musx', matching rpatters1-installs rather than rpatters1-main. Surveyed without --sniff-content and without archives: every source is named *.mus and committed loose. Unlike the other two surveys the corpus itself ships with the repository, so this row can be re-derived from a clone: run scripts/inventory.py against tests/evidence with the export convention above, which needs no private configuration. The conf that lets ./regenerate.sh drive it alongside the other two lives under the ignored private/ tree like theirs, and holds nothing private. It is tiny by design, so it settles questions about specific eras and must never be read as a percentage. Re-surveyed 2026-08-17 after F2012-lyric-punct.mus was added and the count rose from 69 to 70. That fixture is the only specimen in any survey that carries a lyric punctuation ignore list: Finale writes the list as a variable-length tail on selector 57 and only when it differs from the stock set, so all 1,189 companion-backed documents of the reference corpus are silent on it and no corpus of any size could have located it.
